basics.name: Diogo M. Camacho
basics.summary: Scientific leader and builder at the frontier of AI and biology. Pi-shaped (deep in computational biology and ML, broad across the rest), with 15+ years leading computational teams across pharma, venture-backed biotech, and translational research.

summary_highlights.text: Built and scaled computational organizations across three evolving ventures (Rheos, Cellarity, Abiologics), each from an undefined early mandate to a functioning platform team. Comfortable owning technical direction before the path is clear.
Shipped AI platforms across the discovery lifecycle: patient-stratification algorithms, active-learning frameworks, and agentic systems spanning target ID through preclinical validation.
Recruit and develop computational leaders: hiring, mentorship, succession planning, and the executive searches that fill senior gaps. Scaled from first hire to a 25-person group at Cellarity.

Board and VC interface across multiple companies. Secured >$2.4M in competitive DARPA and NIH funding; 6 patents and 20+ publications (7,000+ citations) across computational biology, ML, and synthetic biology.

work.context: Computational and AI strategy across Pioneering Business Units; embedded in explorations, ProtoCos, and NewCos to establish novel bioplatforms.

highlights.text: AI lead on the founding team of FL111, owning computational efforts from exploration through seed funding. Advisory roles on FL106, FL108, and FL115 across the same stages.
Computational and data strategy for multiple seed-stage ventures (FL110, FL111, FL121). Built their platform capabilities and set the technical direction for early programs.
Built agentic AI systems for drug discovery and direct-to-consumer health applications across the Flagship portfolio.
Recruited and retained computational science leaders across five portfolio companies (Ampersand, FL121, FL122, FL110, FL115).

embedded.context: AI-driven D-amino acid mini-binder design platform; agentic AI for target identification and prioritization; led AI transformation for scientific and operational excellence.

highlights.text: Lead the computational sciences function for a D-amino acid therapeutic platform: AI-first design strategy, operations, and execution.
Made active learning the core experimental-design approach for mini-binder optimization, so candidate prioritization across the DBT cycle runs on data, not intuition.
Built and deployed agentic AI systems for target identification, prioritization, and competitive intelligence.
Own team growth and function end to end: hiring, performance management, budgeting, and executive search.
Independent consultancy advising biotech and pharma on computational biology strategy, AI platform development, and data governance.

work.position: Vice President, Computational and Data Sciences
work.context: Transformed the computational platform for cell-behavior medicine discovery; advanced AI/ML models for small-molecule identification supporting pharma partnerships.

highlights.text: On the R&D Leadership Team, reporting to the CSO. Shaped corporate strategy where the computational platform met therapeutic portfolio direction.
Scaled and led a 25-person computational organization across bioinformatics, ML, and computational biology, with teams in Boston and Germany.
Directed platform strategy and operations end to end. Put Cellarity's computational capabilities into R&D programs and into the investor narrative for fundraising.
Primary computational interface for the board, founding VC partners, and external collaborators on platform differentiation and roadmap.

work.position: Senior Director, Computational Biology and Bioinformatics
work.context: Built the MetPM computational platform and the MetKG proprietary knowledge graph; contributed to the Series B investor narrative.

highlights.text: Set the computational precision-medicine strategy for immunometabolism drug discovery: how patient stratification and multi-omics data would drive program decisions.
Defined and implemented Rheos' AI and data strategy with Research Informatics, across discovery and translational programs.
Built the MetPM platform and MetKG knowledge graph: patient-stratification algorithms and multi-omics tooling adopted across the pipeline.
Presented computational strategy to the board and pharma partners; contributed to the Series B investor narrative.

work.context: Founded a new Wyss group bringing AI/ML capabilities to drug discovery, synthetic biology, and systems biology; Co-PI on key federal grants.

highlights.text: Founded and led the Predictive BioAnalytics Initiative, a new ML/AI function embedded in translational science. Set the research strategy, secured the funding, and built the team from scratch.
Raised >$2.4M in competitive DARPA and NIH grants as Co-PI.
Co-led the computational side of host immune-tolerance research: transcriptomics that identified infection-response pathways, later validated experimentally and published in Advanced Science.
Directed and mentored interdisciplinary teams (staff scientists, postdocs, graduate students, interns) across synthetic biology, systems biology, and ML.
